title: The steps
text: The Python and R scripts do the same steps. This page explains the steps in plain words. The next pages show the code.

title: The steps
text:
Three Darwin Core ideas
An event is a place and a time. One event is the whole survey. Each photo is also an event, because each photo has its own position.
An occurrence is one taxon in one photo. If a photo has Ulva and Chlorophyta, it has two occurrences. The occurrence records how many points hit that taxon.
A measurement is a number about an event or an occurrence. Here, a measurement can be percent cover, a point count, the quadrat area, or the camera height.

title: The steps
text:
The six steps

1. Read the files
The script reads two files:

metadata.csv: one row for each photo.
annotations.csv: one row for each point in each photo.

It does not read a config file. The settings are at the top of the script.


2. Make the events
The script makes one parent event for the survey. Then it makes one child event for each photo. The parent event uses the centre of all photo positions. Each child event uses its own photo position. The child event ID includes the field group, because the same frame number can appear in more than one group.


3. Check the points
Each photo must have 100 points. The script stops if a photo has a different number. This keeps the percent cover clear: 1 point = 1 percent.


4. Make the occurrences
The script groups the points by photo and by CoralNet label. It counts the points for each group. If the group is a taxon, the script writes an occurrence. If the group is substrate, unclear, or a generic lichen label, the script leaves it out. If the group is a functional macroalga group, the script leaves it out for now.
The percent cover is:
points for this taxon / all points in the photo * 100


5. Make the measurements
For each photo, the script writes three measurements:

quadrat area
camera height
number of points that are not a taxon

For each occurrence, it writes four measurements:

percent cover
number of points
machine-annotated points
human-annotated points



6. Write the archive
The script writes four text files and one zip file. meta.xml tells the IPT which column is which Darwin Core term.

title: The steps
text:
What stays out

No depth. The quadrats are above water.
No time of day. Only the date is known.
No absence records. Only detected taxa are written.
No image files or image URLs.
No EML. EML is added later in the IPT.

See Notes for more.

5. Count the points
The script groups the points by image and label. It counts all points. It also finds the points made by CoralNet’s automated classifier, which is stored as robot.
groups = {}
for row in annotations:
    key = (row["Name"], row["Label code"])
    groups.setdefault(key, []).append(row)

for (image, code), rows in groups.items():
    points = len(rows)
    machine = sum(1 for row in rows if row["Annotator"] == "robot")
    human = points - machine
    annotators = sorted({
        "CoralNet machine learning annotator"
        if row["Annotator"] == "robot"
        else row["Annotator"]
        for row in rows
    })
The robot value is written as CoralNet machine learning annotator in identifiedBy. Human usernames are kept as they are. When a row has more than one value, the values are separated by |.

def make_zip():

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Convert CoralNet photoquadrat files into a Darwin Core Archive for OBIS.

This is one file on purpose. Read it from top to bottom.
It uses only the Python standard library.
The file looks long because it lists every column and every taxon.
The conversion itself is six short steps.
Change the settings and the TAXA table, then run:

    python3 convert.py

It reads:
    data/metadata.csv
    data/annotations.csv

It writes:
    output/event.csv
    output/occurrence.csv
    output/extendedmeasurementorfact.csv
    output/meta.xml
    output/README.txt
    output/p2p-azores-2026.zip
"""

import csv
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

# =============================================================================
# SETTINGS
# Change these values for a new survey.
# =============================================================================

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# points until the group agrees on a taxonomic mapping.

# =============================================================================
# COLUMN ORDER
# The same order is used in the CSV files and in meta.xml.
# =============================================================================

EVENT_COLUMNS = (
    "eventID parentEventID eventDate year month day country countryCode "
    "stateProvince island locality locationID waterBody habitat "
    "decimalLatitude decimalLongitude geodeticDatum "
    "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters coordinatePrecision verbatimLatitude "
    "verbatimLongitude georeferenceProtocol locationRemarks samplingProtocol "
    "sampleSizeValue sampleSizeUnit samplingEffort fieldNumber "
    "eventRemarks"
).split()

OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS = (
    "occurrenceID eventID scientificName scientificNameID "
    "scientificNameAuthorship taxonRank kingdom phylum class order family "
    "genus basisOfRecord occurrenceStatus organismQuantity "
    "organismQuantityType identifiedBy recordedBy identificationRemarks "
    "occurrenceRemarks"
).split()

EMOF_COLUMNS = (
    "eventID occurrenceID measurementID measurementType measurementTypeID "
    "measurementValue measurementUnit measurementUnitID measurementMethod "
    "measurementRemarks"

# =============================================================================
# SMALL HELPERS
# =============================================================================


def read_rows(path):
    """Read a CSV file into a list of dictionaries."""
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


def write_rows(rows, columns, path):
    """Write a list of dictionaries as a CSV file."""
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(
            handle,
            fieldnames=columns,
            lineterminator="\n",
            extrasaction="ignore",
        )
        writer.writeheader()
        for row in rows:
            writer.writerow({column: row.get(column, "") for column in columns})


def six(value):
    """Format a latitude or longitude with 6 decimal places."""
    return f"{float(value):.6f}"


def survey_id(date):
    """The identifier shared by the survey event and all its quadrats."""
    return ":".join(
        [
            PROJECT_CODE,
            date.replace("-", ""),
            COUNTRY_ID_CODE,
            ISLAND_CODE,
            SITE_CODE,
            STRATA,
        ]
    )


def group_code(group):
    """Turn 'Group_1' into 'G1' for use in an event ID."""
    return group.replace("Group_", "G")


def frame_from_name(image_name):
    """Use the last four characters of the image name as the frame code."""
    stem = Path(image_name).stem
    frame = stem.split("_")[-1][-4:]
    if not frame.isdigit():
        raise SystemExit(f"Cannot find a 4-digit frame number in {image_name!r}")
    return frame


def measurement(event_id, occurrence_id, name, mtype, value, unit,
                unit_id="", type_id="", method="", remarks=""):
    """Build one eMoF row. Empty fields stay empty."""
    return {
        "eventID": event_id,
        "occurrenceID": occurrence_id,
        "measurementID": f"{occurrence_id or event_id}:{name}",
        "measurementType": mtype,
        "measurementTypeID": type_id,
        "measurementValue": value,
        "measurementUnit": unit,
        "measurementUnitID": unit_id,
        "measurementMethod": method,
        "measurementRemarks": remarks,
    }


# =============================================================================
# STEP 1: EVENTS
# One parent event for the survey, then one child event per photo.
# =============================================================================


def build_events(metadata):
    dates = sorted({row["Date"] for row in metadata})
    if len(dates) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            "This script expects one survey date. "
            f"Found these dates: {', '.join(dates)}"
        )
    date = dates[0]
    year, month, day = date.split("-")
    survey = survey_id(date)

    groups = sorted({row["Group"] for row in metadata})
    missing_groups = [group for group in groups if group not in RECORDED_BY]
    if missing_groups:
        raise SystemExit(
            "These field groups do not have a recordedBy string: "
            + ", ".join(missing_groups)
        )

    latitudes = [float(row["Latitude"]) for row in metadata]
    longitudes = [float(row["Longitude"]) for row in metadata]

    # These fields are the same for the parent and the child events.
    common = {
        "eventDate": date, "year": year, "month": month, "day": day,
        "country": COUNTRY, "countryCode": COUNTRY_CODE,
        "stateProvince": STATE_PROVINCE, "island": ISLAND,
        "locality": LOCALITY, "locationID": LOCATION_ID,
        "waterBody": WATER_BODY, "habitat": HABITAT,
        "geodeticDatum": GEODETIC_DATUM,
        "georeferenceProtocol": GEOREFERENCE_PROTOCOL,
        "samplingProtocol": SAMPLING_PROTOCOL,
    }

    # The parent event is a summary of the whole survey.
    events = [{
        **common,
        "eventID": survey,
        "parentEventID": "",
        "decimalLatitude": six(sum(latitudes) / len(latitudes)),
        "decimalLongitude": six(sum(longitudes) / len(longitudes)),
        "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters": str(PARENT_UNCERTAINTY_M),
        "coordinatePrecision": "0.000001",
        "verbatimLatitude": "",
        "verbatimLongitude": "",
        "locationRemarks": (
            "Coordinates are the centre of the child photoquadrats. "
            "Each child event has its own camera position."
        ),
        "sampleSizeValue": str(len(metadata)),
        "sampleSizeUnit": "quadrats",
        "samplingEffort": f"{len(metadata)} photoquadrats",
        "fieldNumber": "",
        "eventRemarks": (
            f"One survey event with {len(metadata)} photoquadrats. "
            "Sampled above water; depth not recorded."
        ),
    }]

    image_events = {}
    for row in metadata:
        image = row["Name"]
        event_id = (
            f"{survey}:{group_code(row['Group'])}:IMG{frame_from_name(image)}"
        )
        image_events[image] = event_id
        height = row.get("Height (cm)") or str(CAMERA_HEIGHT_CM)
        events.append({
            **common,
            "eventID": event_id,
            "parentEventID": survey,
            "decimalLatitude": six(row["Latitude"]),
            "decimalLongitude": six(row["Longitude"]),
            "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters": str(COORDINATE_UNCERTAINTY_M),
            "coordinatePrecision": "0.000001",
            "verbatimLatitude": row["Latitude"],
            "verbatimLongitude": row["Longitude"],
            "locationRemarks": "",
            "sampleSizeValue": str(POINTS_PER_IMAGE),
            "sampleSizeUnit": "points",
            "samplingEffort": f"{POINTS_PER_IMAGE} points",
            "fieldNumber": image,
            "eventRemarks": (
                f"Photoquadrat {image}; camera height {height} cm; "
                f"camera {CAMERA}; "
                f"field group {row.get('Group', '')}; "
                f"strobes {row.get('Strobes', '')}; "
                f"comment: {row.get('Comments', '')}. "
                "Sampled above water; depth not recorded."
            ),
        })

    return events, image_events


# =============================================================================
# STEP 2: OCCURRENCES
# One occurrence for each taxon found in each photo.
# =============================================================================


def build_occurrences(annotations, image_events, metadata):
    total_points = {}
    for row in annotations:
        total_points[row["Name"]] = total_points.get(row["Name"], 0) + 1
    for image, total in total_points.items():
        if total != POINTS_PER_IMAGE:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"{image} has {total} points, but the script expects "
                f"{POINTS_PER_IMAGE}."
            )

    known = set(TAXA) | set(EXCLUDED) | set(DEFERRED)
    unknown = sorted({row["Label code"] for row in annotations} - known)
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit(
            "These CoralNet labels are not in the script: " + ", ".join(unknown)
        )

    # Check that each label ID still belongs to the expected code.
    for row in annotations:
        code = row["Label code"]
        if code in TAXA and row["Label ID"] != TAXA[code]["label_id"]:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"Label {code} has ID {row['Label ID']}, "
                f"but the script expects {TAXA[code]['label_id']}."
            )

    # Group the points by image and label.
    groups = {}
    for row in annotations:
        key = (row["Name"], row["Label code"])
        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(row)

    metadata_by_image = {row["Name"]: row for row in metadata}
    image_order = {row["Name"]: index for index, row in enumerate(metadata)}
    taxon_order = {code: index for index, code in enumerate(TAXA)}
    ordered_keys = sorted(
        groups,
        key=lambda key: (image_order[key[0]], taxon_order.get(key[1], 99), key[1]),
    )

    occurrences = []
    for image, code in ordered_keys:
        if code not in TAXA:
            continue

        taxon = TAXA[code]
        rows = groups[(image, code)]
        points = len(rows)
        machine = sum(1 for row in rows if row["Annotator"] == "robot")
        human = points - machine
        annotators = sorted({
            (
                "CoralNet machine learning annotator"
                if row["Annotator"] == "robot"
                else row["Annotator"]
            )
            for row in rows
        })
        total = total_points[image]
        percent = f"{points / total * 100:.2f}"
        event_id = image_events[image]
        occurrence_id = f"{event_id}:aphia-{taxon['aphia']}"
        group = metadata_by_image[image]["Group"]
        recorded_by = RECORDED_BY[group]

        occurrences.append({
            "occurrenceID": occurrence_id,
            "eventID": event_id,
            "scientificName": taxon["name"],
            "scientificNameID": (
                "urn:lsid:marinespecies.org:taxname:" + taxon["aphia"]
            ),
            "scientificNameAuthorship": taxon["authorship"],
            "taxonRank": taxon["rank"],
            "kingdom": taxon["kingdom"],
            "phylum": taxon["phylum"],
            "class": taxon["class"],
            "order": taxon["order"],
            "family": taxon["family"],
            "genus": taxon["genus"],
            "basisOfRecord": (
                "MachineObservation" if machine > 0 else "HumanObservation"
            ),
            "occurrenceStatus": "detected",
            "organismQuantity": percent,
            "organismQuantityType": "percent cover",
            "identifiedBy": "|".join(annotators),
            "recordedBy": recorded_by,
            "identificationRemarks": (
                f"CoralNet label {code} (ID {taxon['label_id']}); "
                f"{points} of {total} points; "
                f"{machine} machine and {human} human annotations."
            ),
            "occurrenceRemarks": (
                f"{percent}% cover from {points} of {total} grid points."
            ),
        })

    return occurrences


# =============================================================================
# STEP 3: MEASUREMENTS
# Three measurements per photo, then four measurements per occurrence.
# =============================================================================


def build_emof(annotations, events, occurrences):
    counts = {}
    machine_counts = {}
    for row in annotations:
        key = (row["Name"], row["Label code"])
        counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        if row["Annotator"] == "robot":
            machine_counts[key] = machine_counts.get(key, 0) + 1

    aphia_to_code = {taxon["aphia"]: code for code, taxon in TAXA.items()}
    excluded_codes = set(EXCLUDED) | set(DEFERRED)
    rows = []
    counts_unit = "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P06/current/UCNT/"

    for event in events:
        if event["sampleSizeUnit"] != "points":
            continue

        image = event["fieldNumber"]
        event_id = event["eventID"]

        # How many points are not mapped to a taxon?
        excluded_total = 0
        parts = []
        for code in sorted(excluded_codes):
            count = counts.get((image, code), 0)
            if count > 0:
                excluded_total += count
                parts.append(f"{code}={count}")

        area = QUADRAT_WIDTH_CM * QUADRAT_HEIGHT_CM / 10000
        rows.append(measurement(
            event_id, "", "quadrat-area", "quadrat area",
            f"{area:.4f}", "square metres",
            "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P06/current/UMSQ/",
            method=(
                f"{QUADRAT_WIDTH_CM} x {QUADRAT_HEIGHT_CM} cm quadrat "
                "specified by the MBON Pole to Pole protocol"
            ),
        ))
        rows.append(measurement(
            event_id, "", "camera-height", "camera height above substrate",
            str(CAMERA_HEIGHT_CM), "centimetres",
            method="Fixed camera mount specified by the protocol",
        ))
        rows.append(measurement(
            event_id, "", "excluded-points",
            "number of points classified as non-taxon",
            str(excluded_total), "counts", counts_unit,
            method=(
                "Count of grid points assigned to labels that are not mapped "
                "to a taxon (substrate, unclear, lichen, or deferred "
                "macroalgae)"
            ),
            remarks="; ".join(parts),
        ))

        for occurrence in occurrences:
            if occurrence["eventID"] != event_id:
                continue

            aphia = occurrence["scientificNameID"].rsplit(":", 1)[-1]
            code = aphia_to_code[aphia]
            points = counts.get((image, code), 0)
            machine = machine_counts.get((image, code), 0)
            human = points - machine
            percent = f"{points / POINTS_PER_IMAGE * 100:.2f}"
            occurrence_id = occurrence["occurrenceID"]

            rows.append(measurement(
                event_id, occurrence_id, "percent-cover", "percent cover",
                percent, "percent",
                "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P06/current/UPCT/",
                "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P01/current/PCOVRCK1/",
                "Point intercept on a 100-point grid; percent cover = "
                "points assigned to the taxon / total points x 100",
            ))
            rows.append(measurement(
                event_id, occurrence_id, "points", "number of points",
                str(points), "counts", counts_unit,
                method="Count of grid points assigned to the label in CoralNet",
            ))
            rows.append(measurement(
                event_id, occurrence_id, "machine-points",
                "machine-annotated points",
                str(machine), "counts", counts_unit,
                method=(
                    "Count of points whose CoralNet annotator is the "
                    "automated classifier"
                ),
            ))
            rows.append(measurement(
                event_id, occurrence_id, "human-points",
                "human-annotated points",
                str(human), "counts", counts_unit,
                method="Count of points annotated by a person in CoralNet",
            ))

    return rows


# =============================================================================
# STEP 4: WRITE THE ARCHIVE
# =============================================================================


def write_meta_xml():
    """Write the Darwin Core Archive descriptor."""
    def fields(columns):
        return "\n".join(
            f'    <field index="{index}" '
            f'term="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/{name}" />'
            for index, name in enumerate(columns)
        )

    xml = f"""<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<archive xmlns="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/text/">
  <core encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="
" fieldsEnclosedBy=""" ignoreHeaderLines="1" rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Event">
    <files><location>event.csv</location></files>
    <id index="0" />
{fields(EVENT_COLUMNS)}
  </core>
  <extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="
" fieldsEnclosedBy=""" ignoreHeaderLines="1" rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Occurrence">
    <files><location>occurrence.csv</location></files>
    <coreid index="1" />
{fields(OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS)}
  </extension>
  <extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="
" fieldsEnclosedBy=""" ignoreHeaderLines="1" rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/MeasurementOrFact">
    <files><location>extendedmeasurementorfact.csv</location></files>
    <coreid index="0" />
{fields(EMOF_COLUMNS)}
  </extension>
</archive>
"""
    (OUTPUT_DIR / "meta.xml").write_text(xml, encoding="utf-8")


def write_readme():
    """Write a short README that travels inside the zip file."""
    recorded_by = "\n".join(
        f"  {group}: {RECORDED_BY[group]}" for group in sorted(RECORDED_BY)
    )
    text = f"""CoralNet to Darwin Core Archive

Dataset: MBON Pole to Pole photoquadrats, Azores, 2026
Recorded by:
{recorded_by}

Files:
  event.csv                       one survey event and one event per photo
  occurrence.csv                  one row per taxon in one photo
  extendedmeasurementorfact.csv   cover, point counts, and quadrat details
  meta.xml                        Darwin Core Archive descriptor

Open meta.xml in the IPT, or unzip this folder and use the files directly.
"""
    (OUTPUT_DIR / "README.txt").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def make_zip():
    """Put the five archive files into one zip file."""
    name = "p2p-azores-2026.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(
        OUTPUT_DIR / name, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
    ) as archive:
        for filename in [
            "event.csv",
            "occurrence.csv",
            "extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
            "meta.xml",
            "README.txt",
        ]:
            archive.write(OUTPUT_DIR / filename, arcname=filename)
    return name


def main():
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    metadata = read_rows(INPUT_DIR / "metadata.csv")
    annotations = read_rows(INPUT_DIR / "annotations.csv")
    print(f"Read {len(metadata)} images and {len(annotations)} points.")

    events, image_events = build_events(metadata)
    print(f"Built {len(events)} event rows (1 survey + {len(metadata)} photos).")

    occurrences = build_occurrences(annotations, image_events, metadata)
    print(f"Built {len(occurrences)} occurrence rows.")

    emof = build_emof(annotations, events, occurrences)
    print(f"Built {len(emof)} measurement rows.")

    if len({row["eventID"] for row in events}) != len(events):
        raise SystemExit("Duplicate eventID found.")
    if len({row["occurrenceID"] for row in occurrences}) != len(occurrences):
        raise SystemExit("Duplicate occurrenceID found.")

    write_rows(events, EVENT_COLUMNS, OUTPUT_DIR / "event.csv")
    write_rows(occurrences, OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS, OUTPUT_DIR / "occurrence.csv")
    write_rows(emof, EMOF_COLUMNS, OUTPUT_DIR / "extendedmeasurementorfact.csv")
    write_meta_xml()
    write_readme()
    zip_name = make_zip()

    print("Wrote:")
    for name in [
        "output/event.csv",
        "output/occurrence.csv",
        "output/extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
        "output/meta.xml",
        f"output/{zip_name}",
    ]:
        print("  " + name)
    print("Done.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: Notes and limits
text: This example covers one survey. These notes explain what it does and what it does not do.

title: Notes and limits
text:
The survey

The script expects one survey date, one site, and one tidal level.
The example has four field groups.
Each photo must have 100 points.
The camera is the OM System Tough TG-7; the metadata uses the short name TG-7.
The GPS positions come from the camera’s built-in GPS.
Photo events use a 1 metre position uncertainty.
The parent event uses 500 metres because it represents the full beach.
The script stops if a label is not in the TAXA, EXCLUDED, or DEFERRED lists.

title: Notes and limits
text:
The parent event
The parent event is a summary. Its latitude and longitude are the centre of the 207 photo positions. It is not a real sampled point. The child events are the real photo positions. Each child event ID includes its field group, because frame numbers repeat across groups.

title: Notes and limits
text:
Names
recordedBy is free text at the top of the script. There is one string for each field group. It is written to the occurrence table, not the event table. Each occurrence uses the string for its photo’s group.
identifiedBy lists the CoralNet usernames for human annotations. The CoralNet robot value is written as CoralNet machine learning annotator. A mixed row can have more than one name, separated by |.
Multi-value Darwin Core strings in this archive use | as the separator, not ;.

About Imported
Imported is a value in the CoralNet Annotator column, not a person’s username. It means the annotations were added to CoralNet by an import process rather than entered one by one under a user account. The export does not preserve the original person’s username for those points.
In the earlier 523-photo file, Imported covered 7,955 points. It is not in the current 2026-only file, so the current archive needs no special handling for it.
If Imported appears in a future export, do not treat it as robot. The safe choices are to keep the word Imported in identifiedBy as provenance, or to replace it with CoralNet imported annotation and explain that choice in identificationRemarks.
occurrenceStatus is detected on every row. notDetected is the other Darwin Core value, but no absence rows are written.

title: Notes and limits
text:
What is not here

No depth. The quadrats are above water.
No time of day. Only the date is known.
No absence records. A taxon that was not found has no row.
No image files or image URLs.
No EML. Add EML in the IPT.
No associatedMedia column. Add it when stable image URLs exist.

title: Notes and limits
text:
Decisions to review

CIRRIPE is mapped to Chthamalus stellatus (AphiaID 106231).
RVL has two points in two images.
FUCUS, G.griffith, LIQYELLLOW, and gastropod use the WoRMS matches listed in The data.
LICHEN is left out because it is a generic lichen label, not one taxon.
MAF and MAEN are deferred because they are functional groups, not taxa.
SC and Unc are left out.
Coordinates are rounded to 6 decimal places.
Photo events use 1 metre position uncertainty; the parent event uses 500 metres.

title: CoralNet to Darwin Core
text:
This website shows how to turn CoralNet files into Darwin Core.
The files come from photoquadrats on a rocky shore. The survey used the MBON Pole to Pole method. People and a computer marked the organisms in each photo in CoralNet.
Darwin Core is a common table format for biodiversity data. OBIS uses Darwin Core for its data archive.
This example is from the Azores in 2026. It has 207 photos and 20,700 points. The photos come from four field groups. The conversion makes 208 events, 504 occurrences, and 2,637 measurements.

#

# It uses only base R.
# The file looks long because it lists every column and every taxon.
# The conversion itself is six short steps.
# Change the settings and the TAXA table, then run:
#
#     Rscript convert.R
#
# It reads:
#     data/metadata.csv
#     data/annotations.csv
#
# It writes:
#     output/event.csv
#     output/occurrence.csv
#     output/extendedmeasurementorfact.csv
#     output/meta.xml
#     output/README.txt
#     output/p2p-azores-2026.zip

# =============================================================================
# SETTINGS
# Change these values for a new survey.
# =============================================================================

# Run the script from the project folder.

INPUT_DIR <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "data")

  "https://marinebon.org/p2p/"
)

GEODETIC_DATUM <- "WGS84"

# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================

TAXA <- list(
  CHLOROPHY = list(

  ),

  ),

  ),

  ),
  gastropod = list(
    label_id = "353", name = "Gastropoda", aphia = "101",
    authorship = "Cuvier, 1795", rank = "class",
    kingdom = "Animalia", phylum = "Mollusca",
    class = "Gastropoda", order = "", family = "", genus = ""
  )
)

# These labels are not taxa, so they are not written as occurrences.
EXCLUDED <- c("SC", "Unc", "LICHEN")

# These are functional groups, not single taxa. They are counted as non-taxon
# points until the group agrees on a taxonomic mapping.
DEFERRED <- c("MAF", "MAEN")

# =============================================================================
# COLUMN ORDER
# The same order is used in the CSV files and in meta.xml.
# =============================================================================

EVENT_COLUMNS <- c(
  "eventID", "parentEventID", "eventDate", "year", "month", "day",
  "country", "countryCode", "stateProvince", "island", "locality",
  "locationID", "waterBody", "habitat", "decimalLatitude",
  "decimalLongitude", "geodeticDatum", "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters",
  "coordinatePrecision", "verbatimLatitude", "verbatimLongitude",
  "georeferenceProtocol", "locationRemarks", "samplingProtocol",
  "sampleSizeValue", "sampleSizeUnit", "samplingEffort", "fieldNumber",
  "eventRemarks"
)

OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS <- c(
  "occurrenceID", "eventID", "scientificName", "scientificNameID",
  "scientificNameAuthorship", "taxonRank", "kingdom", "phylum", "class",
  "order", "family", "genus", "basisOfRecord", "occurrenceStatus",
  "organismQuantity", "organismQuantityType",
  "identifiedBy", "recordedBy", "identificationRemarks", "occurrenceRemarks"
)

EMOF_COLUMNS <- c(
  "eventID", "occurrenceID", "measurementID", "measurementType",
  "measurementTypeID", "measurementValue", "measurementUnit",
  "measurementUnitID", "measurementMethod", "measurementRemarks"
)

# =============================================================================
# SMALL HELPERS
# =============================================================================

read_table <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
           stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
}

csv_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  needs_quotes <- grepl('[",\n]', x)
  x[needs_quotes] <- paste0('"', gsub('"', '""', x[needs_quotes],
                                      fixed = TRUE), '"')
  x
}

write_csv <- function(data, path) {
  lines <- c(
    paste(csv_escape(names(data)), collapse = ","),
    apply(data, 1, function(row) paste(csv_escape(row), collapse = ","))
  )
  writeLines(lines, path, useBytes = TRUE)
}

rows_to_df <- function(rows, columns) {
  data <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(rows, function(row) {
      as.data.frame(row, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
  )
  data[, columns, drop = FALSE]
}

six <- function(value) {
  sprintf("%.6f", as.numeric(value))
}

survey_id <- function(date) {
  paste(
    PROJECT_CODE, gsub("-", "", date), COUNTRY_ID_CODE, ISLAND_CODE,
    SITE_CODE, STRATA, sep = ":"
  )
}

group_code <- function(group) {
  gsub("Group_", "G", group, fixed = TRUE)
}

frame_from_name <- function(image_name) {
  stem <- sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", image_name)
  frame <- substr(stem, nchar(stem) - 3, nchar(stem))
  if (!grepl("^[0-9]{4}$", frame)) {
    stop("Cannot find a 4-digit frame number in ", image_name)
  }
  frame
}

measurement <- function(event_id, occurrence_id, name, mtype, value, unit,
                        unit_id = "", type_id = "", method = "",
                        remarks = "") {
  prefix <- if (nzchar(occurrence_id)) occurrence_id else event_id
  list(
    eventID = event_id,
    occurrenceID = occurrence_id,
    measurementID = paste0(prefix, ":", name),
    measurementType = mtype,
    measurementTypeID = type_id,
    measurementValue = value,
    measurementUnit = unit,
    measurementUnitID = unit_id,
    measurementMethod = method,
    measurementRemarks = remarks
  )
}

# =============================================================================
# STEP 1: EVENTS
# One parent event for the survey, then one child event per photo.
# =============================================================================

build_events <- function(metadata) {
  dates <- sort(unique(metadata$Date))
  if (length(dates) != 1) {
    stop("This script expects one survey date. Found: ",
         paste(dates, collapse = ", "))
  }
  date <- dates[[1]]
  date_parts <- strsplit(date, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  survey <- survey_id(date)

  groups <- sort(unique(metadata$Group))
  missing_groups <- setdiff(groups, names(RECORDED_BY))
  if (length(missing_groups) > 0) {
    stop("These field groups do not have a recordedBy string: ",
         paste(missing_groups, collapse = ", "))
  }

  # These fields are the same for the parent and the child events.
  common <- list(
    eventDate = date,
    year = date_parts[1],
    month = date_parts[2],
    day = date_parts[3],
    country = COUNTRY,
    countryCode = COUNTRY_CODE,
    stateProvince = STATE_PROVINCE,
    island = ISLAND,
    locality = LOCALITY,
    locationID = LOCATION_ID,
    waterBody = WATER_BODY,
    habitat = HABITAT,
    geodeticDatum = GEODETIC_DATUM,
    georeferenceProtocol = GEOREFERENCE_PROTOCOL,
    samplingProtocol = SAMPLING_PROTOCOL
  )

  parent <- c(common, list(
    eventID = survey,
    parentEventID = "",
    decimalLatitude = six(mean(as.numeric(metadata$Latitude))),
    decimalLongitude = six(mean(as.numeric(metadata$Longitude))),
    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = as.character(PARENT_UNCERTAINTY_M),
    coordinatePrecision = "0.000001",
    verbatimLatitude = "",
    verbatimLongitude = "",
    locationRemarks = paste(
      "Coordinates are the centre of the child photoquadrats.",
      "Each child event has its own camera position."
    ),
    sampleSizeValue = as.character(nrow(metadata)),
    sampleSizeUnit = "quadrats",
    samplingEffort = paste(nrow(metadata), "photoquadrats"),
    fieldNumber = "",
    eventRemarks = paste(
      "One survey event with", nrow(metadata), "photoquadrats.",
      "Sampled above water; depth not recorded."
    )
  ))

  rows <- list(parent)
  image_events <- character(0)

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(metadata))) {
    row <- metadata[i, , drop = FALSE]
    image <- row$Name
    event_id <- paste0(
      survey, ":", group_code(row$Group), ":IMG", frame_from_name(image)
    )
    image_events[[image]] <- event_id
    height <- row[["Height (cm)"]]
    if (!nzchar(height)) height <- as.character(CAMERA_HEIGHT_CM)

    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c(common, list(
      eventID = event_id,
      parentEventID = survey,
      decimalLatitude = six(row$Latitude),
      decimalLongitude = six(row$Longitude),
      coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = as.character(
        COORDINATE_UNCERTAINTY_M
      ),
      coordinatePrecision = "0.000001",
      verbatimLatitude = row$Latitude,
      verbatimLongitude = row$Longitude,
      locationRemarks = "",
      sampleSizeValue = as.character(POINTS_PER_IMAGE),
      sampleSizeUnit = "points",
      samplingEffort = paste(POINTS_PER_IMAGE, "points"),
      fieldNumber = image,
      eventRemarks = paste0(
        "Photoquadrat ", image, "; camera height ", height, " cm; ",
        "camera ", CAMERA, "; field group ", row$Group, "; ",
        "strobes ", row$Strobes, "; comment: ", row$Comments, ". ",
        "Sampled above water; depth not recorded."
      )
    ))
  }

  list(events = rows_to_df(rows, EVENT_COLUMNS), image_events = image_events)
}

# =============================================================================
# STEP 2: OCCURRENCES
# One occurrence for each taxon found in each photo.
# =============================================================================

build_occurrences <- function(annotations, image_events, metadata) {
  total_points <- table(annotations$Name)
  if (any(total_points != POINTS_PER_IMAGE)) {
    stop("At least one image does not have ", POINTS_PER_IMAGE, " points.")
  }

  known <- c(names(TAXA), EXCLUDED, DEFERRED)
  unknown <- sort(setdiff(unique(annotations[["Label code"]]), known))
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("These CoralNet labels are not in the script: ",
         paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
  }

  # Check that each label ID still belongs to the expected code.
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(annotations))) {
    code <- annotations[["Label code"]][i]
    if (code %in% names(TAXA) &&
        annotations[["Label ID"]][i] != TAXA[[code]]$label_id) {
      stop("Label ", code, " has ID ", annotations[["Label ID"]][i],
           ", but the script expects ", TAXA[[code]]$label_id, ".")
    }
  }

  keys <- unique(annotations[, c("Name", "Label code")])
  keys <- keys[keys[["Label code"]] %in% names(TAXA), , drop = FALSE]
  keys <- keys[order(
    match(keys$Name, metadata$Name),
    match(keys[["Label code"]], names(TAXA)),
    keys[["Label code"]],
    method = "radix"
  ), , drop = FALSE]

  rows <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(keys))) {
    image <- keys$Name[i]
    code <- keys[["Label code"]][i]
    taxon <- TAXA[[code]]
    points <- annotations[
      annotations$Name == image & annotations[["Label code"]] == code, ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
    count <- nrow(points)
    machine <- sum(points$Annotator == "robot")
    human <- count - machine
    annotators <- ifelse(
      points$Annotator == "robot",
      "CoralNet machine learning annotator",
      points$Annotator
    )
    annotators <- sort(unique(annotators), method = "radix")
    total <- as.integer(total_points[[image]])
    percent <- sprintf("%.2f", count / total * 100)
    event_id <- image_events[[image]]
    occurrence_id <- paste0(event_id, ":aphia-", taxon$aphia)
    group <- metadata$Group[match(image, metadata$Name)]
    recorded_by <- unname(RECORDED_BY[[group]])

    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- list(
      occurrenceID = occurrence_id,
      eventID = event_id,
      scientificName = taxon$name,
      scientificNameID = paste0(
        "urn:lsid:marinespecies.org:taxname:", taxon$aphia
      ),
      scientificNameAuthorship = taxon$authorship,
      taxonRank = taxon$rank,
      kingdom = taxon$kingdom,
      phylum = taxon$phylum,
      class = taxon$class,
      order = taxon$order,
      family = taxon$family,
      genus = taxon$genus,
      basisOfRecord = if (machine > 0) {
        "MachineObservation"
      } else {
        "HumanObservation"
      },
      occurrenceStatus = "detected",
      organismQuantity = percent,
      organismQuantityType = "percent cover",
      identifiedBy = paste(annotators, collapse = "|"),
      recordedBy = recorded_by,
      identificationRemarks = paste0(
        "CoralNet label ", code, " (ID ", taxon$label_id, "); ",
        count, " of ", total, " points; ",
        machine, " machine and ", human, " human annotations."
      ),
      occurrenceRemarks = paste0(
        percent, "% cover from ", count, " of ", total, " grid points."
      )
    )
  }

  rows_to_df(rows, OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS)
}

# =============================================================================
# STEP 3: MEASUREMENTS
# Three measurements per photo, then four measurements per occurrence.
# =============================================================================

build_emof <- function(annotations, events, occurrences) {
  counts <- table(annotations$Name, annotations[["Label code"]])
  machine_counts <- table(
    annotations$Name[annotations$Annotator == "robot"],
    annotations[["Label code"]][annotations$Annotator == "robot"]
  )
  count_at <- function(table, image, code) {
    if (code %in% colnames(table) && image %in% rownames(table)) {
      as.integer(table[image, code])
    } else {
      0L
    }
  }

  aphia_to_code <- setNames(
    names(TAXA),
    vapply(TAXA, function(taxon) taxon$aphia, character(1))
  )
  counts_unit <- "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P06/current/UCNT/"
  rows <- list()
  quadrats <- events[events$sampleSizeUnit == "points", , drop = FALSE]

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(quadrats))) {
    event <- quadrats[i, , drop = FALSE]
    image <- event$fieldNumber
    event_id <- event$eventID

    # How many points are not mapped to a taxon?
    excluded_total <- 0
    parts <- character(0)
    for (code in sort(c(EXCLUDED, DEFERRED), method = "radix")) {
      count <- count_at(counts, image, code)
      if (count > 0) {
        excluded_total <- excluded_total + count
        parts <- c(parts, paste0(code, "=", count))
      }
    }

    area <- QUADRAT_WIDTH_CM * QUADRAT_HEIGHT_CM / 10000
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
      event_id, "", "quadrat-area", "quadrat area",
      sprintf("%.4f", area), "square metres",
      "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P06/current/UMSQ/",
      method = paste(
        QUADRAT_WIDTH_CM, "x", QUADRAT_HEIGHT_CM,
        "cm quadrat specified by the MBON Pole to Pole protocol"
      )
    )
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
      event_id, "", "camera-height", "camera height above substrate",
      as.character(CAMERA_HEIGHT_CM), "centimetres",
      method = "Fixed camera mount specified by the protocol"
    )
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
      event_id, "", "excluded-points",
      "number of points classified as non-taxon",
      as.character(excluded_total), "counts", counts_unit,
      method = paste(
        "Count of grid points assigned to labels that are not mapped",
        "to a taxon (substrate, unclear, lichen, or deferred macroalgae)"
      ),
      remarks = paste(parts, collapse = "; ")
    )

    event_occurrences <- occurrences[
      occurrences$eventID == event_id, , drop = FALSE
    ]
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(event_occurrences))) {
      occurrence <- event_occurrences[j, , drop = FALSE]
      aphia <- sub(".*:", "", occurrence$scientificNameID)
      code <- aphia_to_code[[aphia]]
      count <- count_at(counts, image, code)
      machine <- count_at(machine_counts, image, code)
      human <- count - machine
      percent <- sprintf("%.2f", count / POINTS_PER_IMAGE * 100)
      occurrence_id <- occurrence$occurrenceID

      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
        event_id, occurrence_id, "percent-cover", "percent cover",
        percent, "percent",
        "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P06/current/UPCT/",
        "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P01/current/PCOVRCK1/",
        paste(
          "Point intercept on a 100-point grid; percent cover =",
          "points assigned to the taxon / total points x 100"
        )
      )
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
        event_id, occurrence_id, "points", "number of points",
        as.character(count), "counts", counts_unit,
        method = "Count of grid points assigned to the label in CoralNet"
      )
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
        event_id, occurrence_id, "machine-points",
        "machine-annotated points",
        as.character(machine), "counts", counts_unit,
        method = paste(
          "Count of points whose CoralNet annotator is the",
          "automated classifier"
        )
      )
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- measurement(
        event_id, occurrence_id, "human-points",
        "human-annotated points",
        as.character(human), "counts", counts_unit,
        method = "Count of points annotated by a person in CoralNet"
      )
    }
  }

  rows_to_df(rows, EMOF_COLUMNS)
}

write_meta_xml <- function() {
  fields <- function(columns) {
    paste(
      sprintf(
        '    <field index="%d" term="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/%s" />',
        seq_along(columns) - 1,
        columns
      ),
      collapse = "\n"
    )
  }

  xml <- c(
    '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
    '<archive xmlns="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/text/">',
    '  <core encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="
" fieldsEnclosedBy=""" ignoreHeaderLines="1" rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Event">',
    '    <files><location>event.csv</location></files>',
    '    <id index="0" />',
    fields(EVENT_COLUMNS),
    '  </core>',
    '  <extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="
" fieldsEnclosedBy=""" ignoreHeaderLines="1" rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Occurrence">',
    '    <files><location>occurrence.csv</location></files>',
    '    <coreid index="1" />',
    fields(OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS),
    '  </extension>',
    '  <extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="
" fieldsEnclosedBy=""" ignoreHeaderLines="1" rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/MeasurementOrFact">',
    '    <files><location>extendedmeasurementorfact.csv</location></files>',
    '    <coreid index="0" />',
    fields(EMOF_COLUMNS),
    '  </extension>',
    '</archive>'
  )
  writeLines(xml, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "meta.xml"), useBytes = TRUE)
}

make_zip <- function() {
  old_dir <- setwd(OUTPUT_DIR)
  on.exit(setwd(old_dir), add = TRUE)
  unlink("p2p-azores-2026.zip")
  utils::zip(
    "p2p-azores-2026.zip",
    files = c(
      "event.csv", "occurrence.csv", "extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
      "meta.xml", "README.txt"
    ),
    flags = "-j"
  )
  "p2p-azores-2026.zip"
}

main <- function() {
  dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  metadata <- read_table(file.path(INPUT_DIR, "metadata.csv"))
  annotations <- read_table(file.path(INPUT_DIR, "annotations.csv"))
  cat(sprintf("Read %d images and %d points.\n",
              nrow(metadata), nrow(annotations)))

  events <- build_events(metadata)
  cat(sprintf("Built %d event rows (1 survey + %d photos).\n",
              nrow(events$events), nrow(metadata)))

  occurrences <- build_occurrences(
    annotations, events$image_events, metadata
  )
  cat(sprintf("Built %d occurrence rows.\n", nrow(occurrences)))

  emof <- build_emof(annotations, events$events, occurrences)
  cat(sprintf("Built %d measurement rows.\n", nrow(emof)))

  if (anyDuplicated(events$events$eventID)) stop("Duplicate eventID found.")
  if (anyDuplicated(occurrences$occurrenceID)) {
    stop("Duplicate occurrenceID found.")
  }

  write_csv(events$events, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "event.csv"))
  write_csv(occurrences, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "occurrence.csv"))
  write_csv(emof, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "extendedmeasurementorfact.csv"))
  write_meta_xml()
  write_readme()
  zip_name <- make_zip()

  cat("Wrote:\n")
  for (name in c(
    "output/event.csv",
    "output/occurrence.csv",
    "output/extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
    "output/meta.xml",
    paste0("output/", zip_name)
  )) {
    cat("  ", name, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("Done.\n")
}

main()
